chapter: The Pelican band and Ridgley years
title: Guitar-banjo and tenor banjo tunings in the old bands
summary: Early banjoists such as Johnny St. Cyr and Lorenzo Starr used a banjo-guitar before the tenor banjo became popular; he also notes the Pelican band's fame, and Ridgley's move toward Suburban Garden.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: What about banjo, how did they tune them in the old days? Everybody used a four string tenor or a spectrum or five string?

Well I can tell you about that. When the banjo, now when they had banjos in the band like I said, they were using the guitar banjo. Because Johnny, not only Johnny's sincere, there was a couple of other guys around there. A fellow named Lorenzo Starr. They used a banjo guitar. In fact like I said before I started playing professional in 24, before the banjo got popular, that's what they were using. And that thing had a pretty good carrying power. Because I remember there was a guy with Sam Morgan band, that was before Johnny something played with him. Johnny Dave. Johnny Dave, before Johnny Dave. And those guys didn't carry no piano. No sir, they didn't carry no piano. And that thing had a man good carry and those guys really played good chords. You know, as far as their ear training would tell them, see. Yeah. And then like I say, when some of the guys, when them, I don't know why they were just a style I imagine, when they went to the tenor banjo, they tuned, some of them tuned the tenor banjo like the four strings only on the guitar. They played the same chord, but the only thing they didn't have that A and the E string, you see. Then eventually some of them, they just went on after that, they said, well now I want to learn the real tenor banjo. They went to the tenor banjo play. See. Yeah. So this band on the Pelicans stayed together. Well like I said, we created a lot of fame, which we didn't make no record, which was hard to do back in those days. And Maniel, I mean, maybe Ridgely, some kind of way he had a little fall and I with his brother Maniel and we left there and we went to, there was a fellow named, all I know him by name is Jack Sheen, they call him the Coconut King. He opened up a place, he built a place called Suburban Garden. And we went out there, I think that's in the St. Bernard Parish because it's right near the river. Way up there?
